premises: Grain boundaries act as fast diffusion paths that initiate localized amorphization and premelting in nanoparticles.
Higher grain boundary density (smaller grains) enhances atomic diffusion and lowers the effective melting point.
Nanoparticles with smaller grains will show earlier premelting onset and a broader melting transition than larger-grained particles.
The effect is significant in nanoparticles below ~100 nm where grain boundary volume fraction is high.
The proposed mechanism is specific to the Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy system.
